chunks.text: Next we will learn how to pass an array or function like an argument.
We have already studied that there are two ways to pass a variable in a function.
One is pass by value.
In this, whatever changes are made in the function, they do not reflect in the main function or calling function.
Second is by reference.
The property of reference is that whatever changes you have made in the variable, they will reflect in the main function or calling function.
Arrays come under this category.
Whenever we pass them, we pass them by reference.
This is our main function.
This is our small function.
We made an array here.
And gave it to our small function.
If the small function has made some changes in the array.
Here.
So those changes will be visible in our main function.
This is a basic thing.
We will also prove it.
First of all, let's make an array.
Int marks.
Let's store marks of three subjects in this array.
And then let's make another function.
public static void update.
This update function will take our array as an argument.
So let's write int marks here.
We have to follow the same process.
In a function, if there was a normal variable, we would have written int physics, int chemistry.
Here we have to write int marks and then our square brackets.
These square brackets show that we have declared an array.
Now in this function, we will add 1 to all the marks.
That is, we will add 1 to all the marks.
To add that, we run a loop.
This loop will run int i is equal to 0.
i less than the length of the marks.
This loop is very important.
In fact, I would say that this loop is more important than the array function.
Because we will be using this loop again and again in the array.
This loop means that we are going to all the indexes of the array one by one.
First of all, we start with 0 index.
And we go to the end until the length of the array is reached.
So the array of 3 sizes will go to 0, 1, 2.
If the array of 50 sizes, then we will go to 0, 1, 2, 3.
And in the end, we will go to the 49th index.
And every time we will reduce our index to i++.
So this i is the index of our array.
Now we have to update the value of each index by 1.
How to do that?
Marks of 0, in fact, we write marks of i.
What is the value of the marks stored on the ith index?
Its value is its old marks plus 1.
So here we have updated the marks at every place.
So this was our marks.
Here we will call the update function.
Update function in which we will pass our marks array.
Now how to verify?
To verify, we have to print the marks of our array.
Now print marks 0, marks 1, marks 2.
We write this loop again.
So we write the same loop.
To print our marks for int i equals 0, i less than marks.length i++.
So here we will print the marks of our array.
Print marks of i.
Give some space.
And at the end, we write print ln.
So what happened from here?
Used means all the marks will be printed in the same line.
First marks will be printed in the 0th index.
After that, marks of the 1st index will be printed.
After that, marks of the 2nd index will be printed.
And finally, the next line will be printed.
So in the beginning, we know what these marks are.
We will update them.
Then we will see if the marks have actually changed in the main function or not.
So first compile the code in the terminal.
Then run.
So what marks were printed in our main function?
First print was 98.
And originally it was 97.
Then print was 99.
Originally it was 98.
And originally it was 99.
So our function update has updated our marks.
And how did it update?
With the help of call by reference.
Because if call by reference is not there, then the update does not work.
Like if I pass some other variable along with the marks.
I passed int non changeable.
Its value is 5.
So non changeable will not change because it is non changeable.
So I wrote int non changeable.
And I have passed 10 for the value of non changeable.
And if I print this value again.
System.out.println
Then this value will not be the same.
Let's verify it.
In case students have forgotten the small concepts.
This non changeable was printed with 5.
Its value was 10 in the update.
But it did not become 10.
It remained the same in the main function.
But the value of our array has changed.
So this is a very basic concept.
Always remember this when we pass arrays in functions.
Usually what will be the situation?
Either we are performing a function on the elements of the array.
Or we make a dedicated function to print the array.
Because we do not want to write the loop of printing again and again.
So we put the loop in the function once.
In such a situation, arrays are passed by reference.
